assessment.overall_rationale: The two annotation sets largely re-partition the same underlying gene program: right splits left's combined detox+sulfation module into a narrower pure-detox module (R1) and a distinct bile-acid sulfonation/taurine module (R2, which also absorbs Cdo1 from left's nitrogen module), while the lipid droplet/peroxisomal module (L2/R3) remains essentially intact across settings; left's urea-cycle/nitrogen theme (L3) has no direct right-side counterpart beyond the shared Cdo1 gene.

pair_scores.rationale: Both describe the same core Phase I/II CYP450/GST/AKR detox battery in pericentral hepatocytes with near-identical gene overlap, but right narrows scope to exclude the SULT2A bile-acid/steroid sulfation arm that left includes.

Both modules share the SULT2A sulfation genes as a bile-acid/steroid conjugation submechanism, but left frames it as one part of a broader Phase I/II detox battery while right isolates it into a distinct sulfonation+taurine bile-acid axis with Cdo1 added.
Xenobiotic/steroid detoxification and conjugation shares no mechanism, gene, or phenotype with lipid droplet biogenesis and peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation.
Only a single incidental shared gene (Aldh3a2) links lipid droplet/peroxisomal fatty acid catabolism to the CAR/PXR/Nrf2 xenobiotic detox battery, with no shared core mechanism.
Lipid droplet/peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and hepatic bile-acid sulfonation/taurine conjugation are distinct mechanisms with no gene or output overlap.

Both modules center on the same core mechanism—ER lipid droplet loading (Fitm1) plus peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation (Eci2, Hao2, Cyb5b, Sord)—with near-total gene overlap; right adds a polyol-fructose submechanism while left adds a peroxisomal aldehyde/protease-quality-control angle (Aldh3a2, Lonp2) in place of Htatip2.
Sulfur amino acid/urea-cycle nitrogen disposal shares no genes or mechanism with the CYP450/GST xenobiotic detox battery.

Both modules invoke Cdo1's cysteine-to-taurine role feeding bile acid conjugation, but left's core theme is broader nitrogen/urea-cycle disposal (Car5a, Agmat) absent from right, while right's core theme is bile-acid sulfonation (Sult2a8) absent from left.
Nitrogen/ammonia disposal via the urea cycle is mechanistically unrelated to lipid droplet biogenesis and peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation, with no gene overlap.
